nodes.name: Hydrothermal growth of MoO3 on NF
nodes.procedure: A pre-cleaned piece of NF (3 cm × 4 cm × 1 mm) was immersed in the solution of 4.0 mmol ammonium molybdate tetrahydrate, which was dissolved in 75.0 mL ultrapure water, followed by ultrasonication for 30 min. The above solution with NF was transferred to a 90-mL Teflon-lined autoclave and heated at 150 °C for 6 h to obtain three-dimensional flower-like MoO3.

nodes.name: Joule heating of MoO3/NF to Mo@MoOx-JH
nodes.procedure: Then, a piece of MoO3 (1 cm × 1.5 cm × 1 mm) was rapidly heated at 973.1 K through Joule heating method (Hefei in situ technology Co., Ltd. China) for 60 s in Ar-H2 (V1/V2 = 1:9) flow with ramp up rate of 84.4 K s⁻¹ and cool down rate of 361.0 K s⁻¹ to obtain Mo@MoOx-JH on NF.

unit_operations.name: Joule heating reduction
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: rapidly heated at 973.15 K for 60 s in the mixed atmosphere of H2/Ar (V1/V2 = 1:9)

nodes.name: Ru impregnation and Joule heating alloying
nodes.procedure: A piece of Mo@MoOx-JH (1 cm × 1.5 cm) was immersed in Ruthenium (III) chloride solution for 2 min, and taken out and dried in an infrared desiccator. The obtained sample was then heated at 1303.1 K with Joule heating method to achieve RuMo@MoOx-JH, while furnishes ramp up rate of 2010.0 K s⁻¹.

nodes.characterization_summary: RuMo@MoOx-JH and Mo@MoOx-JH show characteristic peaks of tetragonal MoO2 phase at 25.9°, 36.9°, 53.3°, 60.3° and 66.7° corresponding to (110), (101), (211), (310) and (301) facets. No peaks for Ru, Mo or RuMo alloy due to ultralow content.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The crystal structure of as-prepared RuMo@MoOx-JH was verified by X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns as shown in Supplementary Fig. 11. In addition to primary peaks of the underlying nickel foam, the XRD patterns of RuMo@MoOx-JH and Mo@MoOx-JH samples displayed a group of characteristic signals corresponding to the (110), (101), (211), (310) and (301) facets of the tetragonal structured MoO2 phase ... at 25.9°, 36.9°, 53.3°, 60.3° and 66.7°, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Both catalysts maintain three-dimensional flower-shaped structure (3-5 μm) with roughened surface attributed to rapid Joule heating treatment.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images (Fig. 2a, d), the pyrolyzed products remained the three-dimensional flower-shaped structure (3-5 μm) with roughened surface, which was attributed to rapid Joule heating treatment.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS confirms coexistence of Ru, Mo, O elements with low Ru concentration of ~1.73 at.% on RuMo@MoOx-JH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: And the corresponding energy dispersive spectrometer (EDS) confirmed the coexistence of Ru, Mo, O with low Ru concentration of ~1.73 at.% on RuMo@MoOx-JH (Supplementary Fig. 12 and Supplementary Table 1), which was consisted with XRD result.

nodes.characterization_summary: Mo@MoOx-JH shows MoO2 (200) lattice spacing of 2.42 Å and embedded cubic Mo NP (111) of 2.30 Å with ~3 nm particle size. RuMo@MoOx-JH shows Mo2Ru (150) and MoO2 (200) facets with RuMo NAs of average size 3.17 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: According to the high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) (Fig. 2b, c), Mo@MoOx-JH catalyst showed hybrid signals containing tetragonal MoO2 phase (200) and embedded cubic crystal Mo nanoparticle (NP) (111), which corresponded to the measured lattice spacings of 2.42 Å and 2.30 Å, respectively. ... In details, the RuMo NAs with small average size of about 3.17 nm were uniformly on the MoOx in the TEM image of RuMo@MoOx-JH.

nodes.characterization_summary: Atomic-resolution HAADF-STEM verifies Ru atoms in RuMo nanoalloy.
nodes.evidence_snippet: And the atomic-resolution HAADF-STEM image was performed to verify the Ru atom in Supplementary Fig. 13.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX elemental mapping shows homogeneous distribution of Ru and Mo elements in RuMo NA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Besides, the energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) elemental mapping of RuMo NA in Supplementary Fig. 14, 15 indicated the homogeneous distribution of Ru and Mo elements.

nodes.characterization_summary: Geometric phase analysis reveals significant strain impact (ε_xx component) and lattice dislocations in RuMo@MoOx-JH and Mo@MoOx-JH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Meanwhile, the geometric phase analysis (GPA) was performed for the RuMo NA, wherein ε_xx component of strain tensor revealed significant strain impact (Fig. 2i).

nodes.characterization_summary: RuMo@MoOx-JH Mo 3d peaks 228.4 eV (Mo⁰ 3d5/2) and 231.5 eV (Mo⁰ 3d3/2); Ru 3p metallic Ru dominant at 462.3 eV and 484.6 eV (Ru⁴⁺:Ru⁰ = 0.15:1); O 1s at 530.6 eV (OL), 531.9 eV (Ov), 533.3 eV (OH2O). Mo@MoOx-JH shows similar Mo 3d with metallic Mo states.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 3a, Mo 3d5/2 and 3d3/2 peaks located at 238 eV to 228 eV for both samples implied the presence of Mo with a valence state of (0≤Z≤6) after deconvolution. Typically, the Mo⁰ signals (228.4 eV for Mo⁰ 3d5/2 and 231.5 eV for Mo⁰ 3d3/2) at low binding energy could be observed ... In addition, the core-level Ru 3p spectra could be deconvoluted into two states of Ru (Fig. 3b), wherein the dominant peaks of 462.3 eV and 484.6 eV belonged to metallic Ru. ... The O 1s XPS spectrum peaks at 530.6 eV, 531.9 eV and 533.3 eV were characteristics of the formation of lattice oxygen (OL), oxygen vacancy (Ov) and oxygen from adsorbed water (OH2O) (Fig. 3c).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru K-edge XANES shows metallic Ru nature (similar to Ru foil); FT-EXAFS shows Ru-O at ~1.53 Å and Ru-Mo at ~2.42 Å; EXAFS fitting gives Ru-Mo CN=7.01 at 2.71 Å; WT-EXAFS confirms Ru-Mo coordination.
nodes.evidence_snippet: To investigate the atomic coordination environment and valance state of RuMo@MoOx-JH, the Ru K-edge X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAFS) spectra was utilized ... The Ru-Mo coordination environment were identified based on the Mo2Ru model, wherein the CN was 7.01 with the Ru-Mo interatomic distance of 2.71 Å, further confirming the formation of RuMo NAs.

nodes.characterization_summary: RuMo@MoOx-JH shows low dissolved Mo concentration of 2.78 mg L⁻¹ (0-3 h) and 3.57 mg L⁻¹ (9 h) at 200 mA cm⁻² vs 5.85 mg L⁻¹ and higher for Mo@MoOx-JH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For as-synthesized RuMo@MoOx-JH, the low dissolved Mo concentration at 0-3 h range (2.78 mg L⁻¹) manifested effective maintenance of the Mo site (Fig. 5a), which was much lower than Mo@MoOx-JH (5.85 mg L⁻¹).

nodes.characterization_summary: Mo@MoOx-JH shows less oxygen vacancy formation than Mo@MoOx-TG due to ultrashort thermal reduction by rapid Joule heating.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The electron paramagnetic resonance spectra (EPR) was applied to investigate the hydrogen spillover ... It should be noted that the rapid Joule heating for Mo@MoOx-JH resulted in less formation of Ov among MoOx support, which might be caused by the ultrashort thermal reduction.

nodes.characterization_summary: RuMo@MoOx-JH double-layer capacitance Cdl = 389.6 mF cm⁻²; Mo@MoOx-JH Cdl = 227.5 mF cm⁻² in non-Faradaic region.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The double-layer capacitance (Cdl) in non-Faradaic voltage window was examined in KOH solution to investigate the intrinsic catalytic activity. As shown in Supplementary Fig. 23, RuMo@MoOx-JH possessed a Cdl value of 389.6 mF cm⁻², nearly 1.71- and 38.6-fold higher than that of Mo@MoOx-JH (227.5 mF) and NF (10.1 mF) counterparts, respectively.
